stories.headline: Yang Hao-Jen makes Taiwan's senior national team for the first time as Hung Jing-Kai takes the last men's place at the trials
stories.summary: Yang Hao-Jen, 19, came from a game down in his final match to win a first senior national team place for 2027, a day after losing a play-off for one.
body: Yang Hao-Jen has been selected for Taiwan's senior national team for the first time after winning the sixth and final stage of the men's national ranking trials, coming from a game down to beat Lin Chin-Ting 10-12, 11-8, 11-7, 11-9 in his last match.

The 19-year-old First Bank player, ranked 195th in the world, had come within one match of a place a day earlier, beating three national team players in the fifth stage before losing a play-off 3-1 to a 17-year-old. Lin had won a mixed doubles bronze at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar this month.

Yang played 23 matches and 90 games over the six days. "I'm really tired. I've been getting up very early to prepare for matches and I've played so many of them. All I want now is a good sleep," he told the Liberty Times (translated from Chinese). He is next due at the World Youth Championships in Turkey, which start on 21 November.

Hung Jing-Kai, also 19 and the world No 120, won the other place from the final stage, winning his deciding match 11-6, 11-9, 10-12, 11-3, to make the national team for a fourth year running. The trials have also brought back Kao Cheng-Jui, as Eleven [reported on Tuesday](/news/kao-cheng-jui-taiwan-national-team-trials-2026.html), and given the Youth Olympic champion Chen Min-Hsin [the last women's place](/news/chen-min-hsin-taiwan-national-team-trials-2026.html).

stories.headline: Youth Olympic champion Chen Min-Hsin takes the last place in Taiwan's women's national team at the ranking trials
stories.summary: Chen Min-Hsin, 17, who won Taiwan's first Youth Olympic singles gold in Dakar this month, has won a senior national team place for 2027 at the last stage of the trials.
body: Chen Min-Hsin, who won Taiwan's first Youth Olympic Games women's singles gold in Dakar on 6 November, has taken the last place in Taiwan's senior women's national team at the national ranking trials.

The 17-year-old won six matches in a row in the sixth and final stage on Wednesday, finishing with an 11-6, 11-4, 11-5 win over Huang Yu-Chiao, a national team player for nine years. She had failed to win any of the first five stages, losing four times in deciding games and once 3-1 to the chopper Chen Chia-Yi, after only five days at home following the long journey from Senegal.

"I've finally been selected. Thank you to myself for not giving up," she told the Liberty Times (translated from Chinese), adding that the expectations after her gold had left her close to breaking point. It is her second senior national team selection, after missing out last year.

Tsai Yun-En won the same stage without dropping a game to make the national team for a third year running. The trials have also brought Kao Cheng-Jui back into the men's team, as Eleven [reported on Tuesday](/news/kao-cheng-jui-taiwan-national-team-trials-2026.html).

stories.headline: Sonalben Patel wins India's first World Para Table Tennis Championships medal with class 3 bronze in Pattaya
stories.summary: Sonalben Patel lost her women's class 3 semi-final to Italy's Carlotta Ragazzini but takes bronze, India's first medal at the World Para Championships.
body: Sonalben Patel has won India's first ever medal at the World Para Table Tennis Championships, taking bronze in women's singles class 3 in Pattaya, Thailand.
She lost her semi-final 3-1 to Italy's Carlotta Ragazzini on Wednesday, 9-11, 11-6, 7-11, 5-11. There is no bronze medal match, so both beaten semi-finalists take bronze.

Patel had guaranteed the medal on Tuesday by beating Brazil's Thais Fraga Severo 11-9, 11-4, 11-5 in the quarter-finals, after a 12-10, 4-11, 9-11, 11-9, 11-7 win over South Korea's Lee Mi-Gyu, a two-time Asian Para Games medallist, in the last 16.
Bhavina Patel, India's Tokyo 2020 Paralympic medallist, lost in the class 4-5 quarter-finals.

stories.headline: Lucas Didier ends Laurens Devos's 11-year unbeaten run at the World Para Table Tennis Championships
stories.summary: France's Lucas Didier beat Belgium's three-time Paralympic champion Laurens Devos 3-0 in the men's class 9 quarter-finals in Pattaya, Devos's first singles defeat since 2015.
body: Laurens Devos, Belgium's three-time Paralympic champion and the defending world champion, lost a singles match in class competition for the first time in 11 years when France's Lucas Didier beat him 11-6, 11-8, 11-7 in the men's class 9 quarter-finals of the World Para Championships in Pattaya on Wednesday.

The match took about 20 minutes. Devos, 26, the world No 2, had not lost a singles match since the 2015 Belgian Open and had never lost at a world championships. He had won the 2022 world title in Granada and beat Didier 11-9, 11-7, 11-7 in the Paris 2024 Paralympic final; in their 10 previous meetings Didier had won only two games.

Didier, the world No 8, could not follow it up: Britain's Joshua Morizono beat him 3-0 in the semi-finals and meets Australia's Ma Lin in Thursday's final, as Eleven [reports here](/news/world-para-championships-2026-mckibbin-morizono-finals-davies-bronze.html).

It was a hard week for Belgium. Florian Van Acker, the 2016 Paralympic champion, lost in the class 11 quarter-finals to Japan's Takeshi Takemori, and Devos and Marc Ledoux went out of the class 18 doubles in the quarter-finals.

stories.headline: Jörg Roßkopf, Germany's first table tennis world champion, enters Düsseldorf's Sports Hall of Fame
stories.summary: Germany's men's national coach was one of 10 new members inducted into the Sports Hall of Fame Düsseldorf at the city's D.SPORTS Awards on Tuesday night.
body: Jörg Roßkopf, Germany's men's national coach and the country's first table tennis world champion, was inducted into the Sports Hall of Fame Düsseldorf on Tuesday night.

He was one of 10 new members named at the end of the D.SPORTS Awards, the city's annual sports awards, at the Rheinterrasse in Düsseldorf. The hall of fame lists him for table tennis and Borussia Düsseldorf, the club he played for in the Bundesliga. The other inductees included the figure skater Tanja Szewczenko, the fencer Benjamin Kleibrink and the American football player Sebastian Vollmer.

Roßkopf, 57, won the men's doubles world title with Steffen Fetzner in Dortmund in 1989 and the men's World Cup in 1998, and took Olympic doubles silver in 1992 and singles bronze in 1996. He has coached the Germany men's team since 2010, a spell that has covered the peak years of Timo Boll and Dimitrij Ovtcharov and the rise of Dang Qiu.
They join the 10 members inducted at last year's awards, the first to be held.

stories.summary: WTT has given Olympic champions Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha the eighth and last place in the mixed doubles at next month's WTT Finals Hong Kong.
body: Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha will play mixed doubles at the WTT Finals Hong Kong in December after World Table Tennis gave them its wild card on Wednesday. The mixed event has eight pairs: seven qualify through the rankings and the eighth place is WTT's to award.

The Chinese pair, Olympic champions at Paris 2024 and world champions in 2021 and 2023, did not qualify directly. Beijing Daily reported that they are 12th in the mixed doubles standings, and that two other Chinese pairs placed above them, Lin Shidong and Kuai Man and Huang Youzheng and Chen Yi, also missed out on a direct place. WTT's announcement described Wang and Sun as one of the finest mixed doubles partnerships the sport has had.

They reached the final in Hong Kong last year, beating Sora Matsushima and Miwa Harimoto 3-0 in the semi-final, but lost the title 11-9, 11-8, 11-6 to South Korea's Lim Jonghoon and Shin Yubin, with Sun struggling with injury.

Wang has played little since the Asian Games in September: he returned from injury at WTT Champions Frankfurt this month and lost to Wen Ruibo in the last 16. Before Hong Kong, China play the Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu, which starts on 29 November.

stories.headline: Kao Cheng-Jui wins back his Taiwan national team place after an injury-hit year, coming from 8-5 down in the final deciding game
stories.summary: Kao Cheng-Jui, who fell to 198th in the world after two injuries, has regained his place in Taiwan's senior national team at the 2027 ranking trials.
body: Kao Cheng-Jui has won back his place in Taiwan's senior national team, a year after losing it, by beating an 18-year-old from the First Bank team 6-11, 11-6, 9-11, 11-2, 11-9 in the last round of the fifth and final stage of the national ranking trials on Tuesday. He trailed 8-5 in the deciding game and won it on his first match point.

The 21-year-old, once ranked as high as 21st in the world, pulled out of last year's trials with a leg injury and so missed the national team for 2026. He returned at the US Smash in June after six months of treatment, joined Kanazawa Port in Japan's T.League, and was injured again at the end of September, missing the China Smash and Taiwan's national championships. He is now the world No 198.

Kao failed to win any of the first four stages of the trials, which ran for five days and 20 matches, and admitted he had thought about giving up after defeat on Monday. "I told myself to hang on a bit longer; at worst I'd come back next year. After all, I had nothing left to lose, so I let it all go," he told the Liberty Times (translated from Chinese). "I gave a lot to get back on court. This is something to show for it."
It is the sixth time he has been selected for the national team.

stories.headline: India's leading players propose new team selection rules after Manika Batra's Asian Games omission and the TTFI suspension
stories.summary: A group of India's top men and women have asked for world rankings, doubles rankings and a reasoned selection committee to decide teams, after Manika Batra was left out of the Asian Games squad.
body: Some of India's leading table tennis players have put forward a new framework for picking national teams, according to a copy of the proposal seen by Sportstar. It follows the row over Manika Batra, who was ranked 51st in the world when she was named only as a reserve for the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, and the Sports Ministry's suspension of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI), the second in four years, with an ad hoc committee now running the sport.

Under the proposal, domestic rankings would count for 50% of a player's selection score, world rankings for 40% and the selection committee's judgment for 10%. World-ranking points would come in brackets, from 40 for players ranked in the top 50 down to four for those ranked 131st to 150th, and the committee would have to record its sporting reasons for using its 10%, especially when players are separated by 10 points or fewer.

The biggest change is for doubles. Pairs ranked in the world's top five would be considered directly, top-eight pairs would go straight in for the World and Asian Championships where separate doubles entries are allowed, and the top five pairs would qualify directly for the Asian and Commonwealth Games, with at least two singles players of each gender. The players also want selection cut-off dates announced 30 days ahead, a domestic doubles ranking and an India B team sent to WTT Feeder events.
The proposal has been put to the TTFI and now the ad hoc committee. Sportstar did not name the players behind it.

stories.headline: Table Tennis England launches One-time Tournament Pass so players can enter a 1-star or 2-star event without a Compete membership
stories.summary: The pass costs £15 for adults and £10 for under-19s and lets non-members and Supporter or Club Play members enter a single eligible tournament through TTE Hub.
body: Table Tennis England has introduced a One-time Tournament Pass, which lets players enter one eligible 1-star or 2-star tournament without taking out an annual Compete or Compete Plus membership.

The pass costs £15 for adults and £10 for under-19s, is sold through TTE Hub and is open to non-members and to Supporter and Club Play members. Each pass covers one specific tournament, whether it lasts one, two or three days, and players can buy as many as they like. Tournament and event entry fees are charged on top.

Results played on a pass count towards the player's ranking and rating, but the ranking is not published while they compete this way. If they later join as a Compete or Compete Plus member, the earlier results stay on their profile.

Existing Compete members get a matching One-time Tournament Top-up, at £10 for adults and £5 for under-19s, which lets them enter one eligible 2-star or 4-star tournament without upgrading to Compete Plus for the whole membership year. For that tournament it also gives them the same insurance cover as Compete Plus.

stories.headline: Jack Hunter-Spivey and Fliss Pickard lose their opening singles at the World Para Championships in Pattaya
stories.summary: Both Britons went out 3-1 on Sunday, Hunter-Spivey to Serbia's Mitar Palikuca in the class 4-5 last 32 and Pickard to France's Morgen Caillaud in the women's class 6 last 16.
body: Britain's singles campaign at the World Para Championships in Pattaya began badly on Sunday, with Jack Hunter-Spivey and Fliss Pickard both beaten 3-1 in their first matches. All the events in Thailand are straight knockouts, so both are out of the singles.

Hunter-Spivey won the first game 11-6 against Serbia's Mitar Palikuca, the world No 6 and a Paris 2024 bronze medallist, and led 3-1 in the second before Palikuca took the next three games 11-5, 11-5, 11-6 in the men's class 4-5 last 32. "It has been a tough year - I fought like I always do and that is all I can do," Hunter-Spivey said.

Pickard lost the first two games 11-8 to France's Morgen Caillaud, 23, in the women's class 6 last 16, took the third 11-8 and recovered from 6-1 to 6-4 in the fourth before losing it 11-7. She said she had changed her equipment six weeks before the championships. "She played very well and she has improved a lot over the last few months," Pickard said.

Six more British players were due to start their singles on Monday, among them Will Bayley, the class 7 world champion and world No 1, who plays China's Yan Shuo or the Netherlands' Yannick Paredis in the quarter-finals. Bayley and Bly Twomey [won mixed doubles bronze](/news/world-para-championships-2026-doubles-bronze-bayley-twomey-ryan-matthews.html) on Saturday. The championships end on Thursday 19 November.

body: Fang Bo, who won WTT Contender Istanbul on Sunday, starts WTT Star Contender Muscat in qualifying, where he plays Turkey's Abdullah Yigenler in the first round on Monday at 2.45pm UK time (6.45pm in Muscat).

Fang, 34, beat South Korea's Kang Dongsoo 4-1 in the Istanbul final for [his first international singles title since 2013](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html), having entered as a wild card ranked 160th in the world. He is seeded 20th in the Muscat qualifying draw. Yigenler, 27, is ranked 177th and seeded 23rd.

The former China international retired in 2021 and returned this year playing for Kazakhstan. China's Tang Yiren, Sun Yang, Zhai Jiale and Quan Kaiyuan are also in Monday's men's qualifying at the Sultan Qaboos Sport Complex, and the tournament runs to the finals on Saturday 21 November.

body: Nittetsu Butsuryu Blazers won the men's first division and Chugoku Electric Power took the women's title at the Japan Table Tennis League's 100th tournament, the second-half event at Hiroshima Sun Plaza Hall from 11 to 15 November.

Chugoku Electric Power, playing in their home city, were unbeaten after five ties and sealed the women's title on Saturday, a day before the event ended. It was their first title in four tournaments and puts them top of the league's combined standings for the year.

The men's race went to the last round, with Kyowa Kirin, the Blazers, Meiji University and Caritz Technologies level on four wins and three defeats. Kyowa Kirin, who led on game difference, lost to Kansai Table Tennis Academy, while the Blazers beat Meiji, their fourth player Noda winning the decisive match. Caritz also beat Hino Kingfishers to reach five wins, but the Blazers finished ahead on game ratio.

stories.headline: ETTU Europe Cup: SKST Chodov come from 2-0 down and Quattro Mori Cagliari stay unbeaten as Stage 1 ends
stories.summary: Eight men's clubs reached the Europe Cup last 16 in Varaždin and eight women's clubs reached the quarter-finals in Novi Sad, with four unbeaten in each.
body: The first stage of the ETTU Europe Cup finished on Sunday with eight men's clubs through to the last 16 from Varaždin and eight women's clubs through to the quarter-finals from Novi Sad. SPG Felbermayr Wels, SKST Havirov, CTT Olot and SKST Chodov won their men's groups without losing a tie, and CTT Les Borges Vall, the hosts STK STARR Croatia, Energa Manekin Torun and STK Vyhne also went through.

Chodov finished their perfect run by coming from 2-0 down to beat Alicante TM 3-2. Alberto Lillo and Shoma Nishihara both won in five games for Alicante, before Jakub Zelinka and Antonin Gavlas levelled the tie and Jiri Martinko beat Nishihara 3-2. Havirov did not lose an individual match all weekend, beating STARR Croatia 3-0 on the last day.

In the women's event, ASD Quattro Mori Cagliari, STK Dr. Časl Zagreb, CD Indiana Games and the hosts TTC Novi Sad all finished unbeaten, and Museo de la Almendra Francisco Morales, Son Cladera TTC Mallorca, CSM Constanta and MIRÓ Ganxets also reached the last eight. Cagliari needed Pauline Chasselin and Tania Plaian to win key matches to beat Politechnika Rzeszów 8-6, after Zuzanna Wielgos won twice for the Polish club.

Kotomi Omoda won both her matches as Zagreb beat Mallorca 8-5 in the tie between the top two in Group B, and Novi Sad beat TTV Tulln 8-0. [The first day's results are here](/news/ettu-europe-cup-2026-27-stage-1-day-one-starr-croatia-novi-sad.html).

stories.headline: ETTU Champions League Men: Bogoria Grodzisk Mazowiecki come from behind to win 3-1 at Santa Tecla Nulvi
stories.summary: KS Bogoria Grodzisk Mazowiecki won 3-1 at ASD TT Santa Tecla Nulvi in Sardinia after losing the opening match, taking a lead into the second leg of their last-16 tie in Poland in December.
body: KS Bogoria Grodzisk Mazowiecki beat ASD TT Santa Tecla Nulvi 3-1 in Sardinia on Saturday in the first leg of their ETTU Champions League Men last-16 tie, winning three matches in a row after losing the first.

Stéphane Ouaiche gave the hosts the lead by beating Marek Badowski 11-5, 11-4, 11-2. Miłosz Redzimski levelled against Tommaso Giovannetti, saving the first game 14-12 before losing only eight points in the next two, and Greece's Panagiotis Gionis beat Jordy Piccolin 11-8, 11-7, 11-2. Redzimski then beat Ouaiche 11-9, 11-5, 6-11, 11-5 to finish it.

"We now have an advantage, but we must remain focused. There is still another match to play," said Gionis. Francesco Ara, Santa Tecla's captain and coach, said the club could be satisfied with hosting a Champions League match in their small village for the first time.

The second leg is in Poland in December, with a place in the quarter-finals for the winners. body: Britain won two bronze medals at the World Para Championships in Pattaya on Saturday: Will Bayley and Bly Twomey in the mixed class 14 doubles, and Chris Ryan and Tom Matthews in the men's class 4 doubles. Both pairs won their quarter-finals and lost in the semi-finals, and there is no bronze-medal match.

Bayley and Twomey, who [saved two match points](/news/world-para-championships-2026-day-one-bayley-twomey-save-match-points.html) on Friday, beat the Netherlands' Yannick Paredis and Kelly van Zon 12-10, 11-8, 6-11, 11-6. They then came from two games down against the Thai pair Rungroj Thainiyom and Kanlaya Chaiwut-Kriabklang, but lost the fourth game 14-12 and the decider 11-7. Twomey needed a medical timeout after falling at 6-6 in the fifth. "I think we are as good as any team in the world," Bayley said.

Ryan and Matthews beat Italy's Federico Crosara and Federico Falco 12-10, 9-11, 11-7, 11-5, winning the first game from 10-7 down, before losing 3-0 to South Korea's Kim Hyeon Uk and Jang Yeongjin, the world No 1 pair. "It's an amazing feeling to win a medal at my first World Championships," said Ryan, who took up the sport four years ago after playing wheelchair rugby. Joshua Morizono and Aaron McKibbin withdrew from the men's class 18 doubles because McKibbin was ill.

stories.headline: Bats and gold medal from unified Korea's 1991 world title named as South Korean heritage
stories.summary: Five items from the joint North and South Korean team that beat China to win the women's team title at the 1991 World Championships in Chiba have been named preliminary cultural heritage in South Korea.
body: South Korea's Korea Heritage Service has selected the relics, held by the new National Sports Museum, as preliminary cultural heritage, a status for modern objects less than 50 years old that are judged worth registering as heritage in future. The Korea Sports Promotion Foundation, which runs the museum, announced it on Thursday.

The five items are a bat carrying a handwritten message from North Korea's Yu Sun-bok, a bat signed by the team's 17 players and officials, the women's team gold medal and two bats used by South Korea's Hong Cha-ok. Hong and Han Young-geun donated them to the museum in April. The team, entered as Korea, was the first the two countries had fielded together since the peninsula was divided, and it beat China for the title.

Yu's message, written to Hong, reads: "I am truly glad that, for the first time since the division, we became one in heart and mind and trained and lived together. I will never forget the friendship, trust and love that grew with Cha-ok."

Hong, who also won doubles gold at the 1990 Asian Games and doubles bronze at the Barcelona 1992 Olympics, gave the items as part of the museum's donation drive before it opened on 15 October. Ha Hyung-joo, the foundation's chairman, said the players' friendship had been recognised as national heritage after 35 years. It is the second year running that an item from the museum's collection has been chosen, after a hoop and costume sketches from the Seoul 1988 Olympics became the first preliminary cultural heritage last year.

France's Isa Cok needed 53 minutes, the longest match of the morning, to beat Iran's Mahshid Ashtari, taking the decider 15-13.

stories.summary: China's Ao Hualei lost the first game 11-1 and needed a 16-14 decider to beat Iran's Amin Ahmadian on the opening day of qualifying, and now meets England's Connor Green.
body: Ao Hualei, the runner-up at China's National Championships, came close to going out on the first day of qualifying at WTT Contender Istanbul on Tuesday. He won one point in the first game against Iran's Amin Ahmadian and, after levelling the match, needed extra points in the decider, winning it 16-14 after 43 minutes. Chinese reports said Ao let four match points go and saved two before he closed it out. He plays England's Connor Green, who had a bye, in the next qualifying round.

China's three other players on the opening day won in straight games. Wei Jingming beat Turkey's Ozge Yilmaz 11-5, 11-2, 11-2, Feng Yixuan beat Tiffany Ke of the US 13-11, 11-5, 11-8, and Quan Kaiyuan beat Uzbekistan's Khasanboy Teshaboev 11-6, 11-2, 11-8.

England's Tianer Yu, the world No 358, beat Kazakhstan's Sarvinoz Mirkadirova, ranked 187th, 8-11, 11-5, 11-9, 11-7. Four Turkish players won in front of the home crowd: Sibel Altinkaya beat Slovenia's Lara Opeka in five games, Ibrahim Gunduz beat Spain's Norbert Tauler 11-4 in the decider, Gorkem Ocal beat Denmark's Martin Buch after losing the first game 11-2, and Tugay Yilmaz beat Uzbekistan's Shahbozbek Gulomiddinov 11-3, 11-5, 11-6.

Qualifying finishes on Wednesday, when the remaining places in the main draws are decided. Tom Jarvis and Anna Hursey [go straight into the main draw](/news/tom-jarvis-wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-england.html), and the event runs until Sunday.

stories.headline: Liang Jingkun pulls out of WTT Contender Istanbul days after his comeback in Frankfurt
stories.summary: Liang Jingkun has been taken out of the men's singles and men's doubles at WTT Contender Istanbul, leaving a young Chinese squad to play the event.
body: Liang Jingkun has withdrawn from WTT Contender Istanbul, which starts on Tuesday. WTT's updated entry list, published on Monday, removed him from the men's singles and the men's doubles, where he was due to partner Yuan Licen. No reason was given.

Chen Junsong takes Liang's place in the men's singles main draw. Liang's only tournament since his return from months out was [WTT Champions Frankfurt](/news/wtt-champions-frankfurt-2026-day-three-review-results-highlights.html), where he came in as a late replacement and lost 3-2 to Hugo Calderano in the first round after 52 minutes.
Chinese reports said fans linked the decision to preparations for the Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu, which starts on 29 November, but no explanation has come from Liang, the Chinese team or WTT.

China's entry in Istanbul is made up of younger players. Wang Chuqin, Lin Shidong, Sun Yingsha and Wang Manyu were among those who did not enter. Istanbul, which hosts the European Games next summer, is worth 400 ranking points to the singles winners, and the event runs until Sunday.

Liang was not named in China's eight-player squad for the Mixed Team World Cup, which the Chinese Table Tennis Association [announced on Tuesday](/news/mixed-team-world-cup-2026-china-squad-wang-chuqin-sun-yingsha-chen-yi-zhou-qihao.html).

stories.headline: Youth Olympic Games: Lee Seungsoo wins South Korea's first table tennis medal since 2010
stories.summary: South Korea's Lee Seungsoo, 15, beat Hong Kong's Li Ki Ho 4-2 for the men's singles bronze in Dakar, taking the deciding game 15-13.
body: Lee Seungsoo won the Youth Olympic men's singles bronze in Dakar on Thursday, South Korea's first table tennis medal at the Games since the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010.

The 15-year-old won the first three games against Hong Kong's Li Ki Ho, lost the fourth and then a 17-15 fifth, and took the sixth 15-13. In 2010 Kim Donghyun and Yang Haeun won mixed team silver and Yang won women's singles bronze; South Korea had not won a medal at the two Games since.

Lee won all his group matches, came through a seven-game match in the last 16, won his quarter-final 4-1, then lost 4-2 in the semi-final to Japan's Ryusei Kawakami, who went on to win the gold. OSEN reported that Lee had won three of their eight previous meetings on the junior circuit. Lee and Heo Yerim reached the mixed doubles quarter-finals, where they lost to Taiwan's Lin Chin-ting and Chen Min-hsin.

Lee, who won the under-19 boys' singles at WTT Youth Star Contender Gangneung this year, is due to play his first senior event at WTT Contender Istanbul from 10 to 15 November, Sports Kyunghyang reported.

stories.headline: Annett Kaufmann calls for tighter rules on social media platforms during WTT Champions Frankfurt
stories.summary: Germany's Annett Kaufmann, who has received death threats online, has called for internet platforms to be regulated more strictly.
body: Annett Kaufmann has called for tighter regulation of internet platforms, saying abuse of athletes online has become far too normal.

"Hate is not an opinion," the 20-year-old German said at WTT Champions Frankfurt, adding that reading comments about other players sometimes makes her afraid and that words have power. Kaufmann said in March that she had received death threats on social media.

stories.headline: Youth Olympic Games: Ryusei Kawakami and Chen Min-hsin win the singles titles in Dakar
stories.summary: Japan's Ryusei Kawakami beat Colombia's Emanuel Otálvaro and Taiwan's Chen Min-hsin beat Singapore's Loy Ming Ying, both 4-2, in the Youth Olympic singles finals.
body: Japan's Ryusei Kawakami and Taiwan's Chen Min-hsin won the Youth Olympic singles titles in Dakar on Thursday evening, both by four games to two.

Kawakami, the top seed, won the first three games against Colombia's Emanuel Otálvaro, who won the next two before Kawakami closed out the match 11-6. Kawakami, who won the mixed doubles gold with Miku Matsushima on Tuesday, now has two gold medals in Dakar. Otálvaro, 16, had knocked out China's Li Hechen in the quarter-finals.
Chen, 17 and the fifth seed, beat Singapore's 16-year-old Loy Ming Ying, the 10th seed, 4-2. Chen also won the mixed doubles bronze with Lin Chin-ting.

Loy's silver equals Singapore's best Youth Olympic table tennis result, Isabelle Li's runner-up finish at the first Games in Singapore in 2010. "I am happy to be able to fly the Singapore flag," she said, adding that she struggled to return Chen's serve towards the end.

Preuß said Fan's arrival had changed everything from ticketing and merchandise to social media. The club have added two international sponsors, and their matches are shown live in more than 300 cinemas in China.

stories.summary: Desmond Douglas, the 11-time English national champion, has visited the Over-50s Black Men Forum's table tennis health hub in Handsworth, where he grew up.
body: Douglas joined last week's session at Handsworth Wellbeing Centre, played with members and met people he had known growing up in the area. BBC Midlands filmed the session for a report on Midlands Today.

stories.headline: Ken Green, who umpired at the 1977 World Championships in Birmingham, dies aged 93
stories.summary: Ken Green, the international umpire who officiated at the 1977 World Championships in Birmingham, has died aged 93.
body: Green qualified as a national umpire in 1976 and as an ITTF international umpire in 1980. As well as the home world championships in 1977, he umpired at the 1981 edition in Novi Sad, then in Yugoslavia, and at the Commonwealth Championships in Cardiff in 1973 and Edinburgh in 1979.
Born in 1933, he played in the Warrington and Bolton leagues in the north-west before moving to Peterborough, where he died last month after a short illness.
A celebration of his life will be held at St Botolph's Church, Longthorpe, at 1.15pm on Thursday 26 November, followed by committal at Peterborough Crematorium.

The last 16 was played on Thursday, the quarter-finals follow on Saturday after a rest day, and the semi-finals and finals are on Sunday 15 November. Each singles champion receives 10 million won and each runner-up 3 million won.

Jang Hanjae of the Korea Armed Forces Athletic Corps tops the men's standings after winning the third series in Jecheon in August. His 21-year-old teammate Gil Minseok won the fourth series in Jeju on 5 October, beating Cho 11-8, 11-9, 7-11, 14-12 in the final for his first senior singles title.

Choi Hyojoo of Korean Air leads the women after winning the first and third series, and she came through her opening match on Thursday. Lee Daeun, 21, the league's first women's singles champion, is second after taking the fourth series, where she beat Sim Hyunju 3-2 in the final, winning the six-point decider 6-1.

Ito won the opening singles 11-7, 6-11, 9-11, 11-5, 12-10. He then won the doubles with Yan An against Okayama's pairing of Tomokazu Harimoto, the world No 2, and the former Chinese world champion Hao Shuai, 11-6, 11-10. Soma Ono beat Satoshi Aida 11-10, 11-10, 11-10 to seal the win before Harimoto beat Ryuusei Kawakami in five games.

Okayama recovered on Sunday, beating Kanazawa Port, the league leaders, 3-1 at the same venue, a shopping centre in Okayama. Matsushima beat Hiromu Kobayashi in five games and Harimoto beat Taisei Matsushita 3-1. Kanazawa stay top on 30 points, level with Ryukyu Asteeda; Kinoshita are third and Okayama fourth.
The men's league resumes on 12 December, when Kinoshita play Shizuoka Jade and Okayama visit T.T Saitama.
